title: crestwave-payments-integration-call-notes-2026-06-25
content:
Call notes: CrestWave Payments - integration kickoff (internal notes)
Date: 2026-06-25
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood PM), Elena Morales (Redwood AE),	Aaron Lim (CrestWave eng lead), Priya Nambiar (CrestWave product), Mark Chen (CrestWave infra)

Context / business goal:
- CrestWave wants to add LLM-assisted dispute triage to their merchant portal (reduce manual review time).
- Primary metric: reduce avg TTR for disputes by 40% and reduce reviewer load during peak by 3x.
- Timeline: pilot w/ 2 merchants in Q3, broader rollout Q4.

Primary asks from CrestWave:
- Hosted API integration to start (fastest path), with option to move to Dedicated later for cost predictability and compliance.
- Need PII controls and support for customer-managed KMS (will require Private or Dedicated with KMS integration).
- Hard latency target for frontend assistant: 150-200ms p50 for short responses; acceptable p95 up to 600ms for heavier prompts.
- Throughput: expect 200 rps peak for pilot (bursty evenings).
- Retention / logs: 90 days of request logs for audit.

Technical notes / gotchas raised:
- CrestWave uses a multi-tenant infra; they cannot send raw PII to hosted endpoints without masking/encryption. They prefer request-level tokenization or field-level hashing before send.
- They have legacy JSON schema for disputes (approx 30 fields). We should map required minimal context fields to limit prompt size.
- Offline evaluation dataset: they have 10k historical disputes (anonymized) ready for quality tests. Need upload instructions/secure transfer.
- Concern about hallucination on policy citations — they need deterministic citations to internal KB. Discussed function-calling style or structured output to include source IDs.
- Cache benefits: noticed many repeated prefixes (merchant ID + dispute type). Suggest prefix caching and per-merchant KV cache to cut cost. Confirm isolation model for Dedicated.

Integration blockers / risks:
- KMS support: CrestWave requires CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) for audit. Hosted API does not currently support CMEK for customer data — requires Private or Dedicated. Need escalation to security if they insist on hosted with CMEK.
- Latency SLO: achieving 150-200ms p50 on hosted with telemetry depends on model choice (we should propose an optimized small-chat model or trimmed context).
- Data transfer: secure SFTP or direct S3 transfer for historical dataset; confirm legal/data team sign-off.

Proposed next steps (internal + with customer):
- Internal (by 2026-06-28): SE draft of minimal context mapping (fields from CrestWave dispute schema) — owner: Maya.
- Internal (by 2026-07-02): Perf/infra quick baseline: test p50/p95 with recommended model on hosted proxy (small model + prefix cache) — owner: Ravi.
- External (by 2026-07-01): Ask CrestWave to share anonymized sample dataset (S3 or SFTP) + schema doc — owner: Elena to coordinate.
- Security check (by 2026-07-05): Confirm CMEK requirements and list options (Hosted w/o CMEK, Dedicated with CMEK, Private) and high-level impact on cost/SLA — owner: Maya + Security (cc: security@redwood.com).
- PoC plan: 3-week pilot with 2 merchants; goal: validate quality and latency. Draft pilot scope after sample data review.

Action items (short):
- Maya: map dispute schema -> minimal prompt fields (due 6/28).
- Ravi: run latency/cost sims with prefix cache (6/30).
- Elena: collect dataset + set up transfer link (7/1).
- Aaron (CrestWave): confirm merchant list and expected peak hours (7/1).
- Security: quick doc w/ CMEK options and requirements (7/5).

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Might recommend starting with a smaller generation model + edit/verify step: model suggests triage labels + rationale; final decision still by human in early pilot. That reduces hallucination risk.
- Consider using structured output (JSON schema) so CrestWave can plug outputs directly into backlog system. Use function-calling or schema enforcement.
- Cost levers: prefix caching per merchant + compact prompts + response token cap. Quantization profiles for Dedicated if they move there.
- Evaluate reranking on cues where model confidence is low. Could run cheap classifier to gate.

Links / refs:
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE:crestwave-integration-v1
- Jira: CS-1729 (CrestWave onboarding)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/integrations/pull/89 (initial schema parser)

End of notes.
